results.title: Why does temperature affect a battery's available capacity?
results.content:
# Why does temperature affect a battery's available capacity?
Temperature is a significant factor in battery performance, shelf life, charging and voltage control.

Even though the battery capacity at high temperatures is higher, battery life is shortened. High temperatures affect the battery's service life according to a common “rule of thumb” or the law of “Arrhenius,” which states that the corrosion rate will be doubled at 10° C. Therefore, the lifetime will be halved per 10° C increase in temperature.

- Fifteen years at 20° C becomes reduced to 7.5 years at 30°C

|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| <30 Min | -20% | -15% | -12% | -8% | -3% | 0% | +5% | +8% | +10% |
| 30-60 Min | -18% | -13% | -11% | -7% | -2% | 0% | +4% | +6% | +8% |
| >60 Min | -16 | -12% | -10% | -6% | -1% | 0% | +3% | +4% | +5% |

A fully charged battery's shelf life will discharge at approximately:

- 2% per month when stored at 8°C/46°F
- 3% per month when stored at 20°C/68°F
- 5% per month when stored at 30°C/86°F
- 10% per month when stored at 40°C/104°F

results.title: What are temperature effects on batteries? - Intercel | Endless Energy
results.content:
Temperature affects battery capacity, charging behaviour and lifetime. Cold temperatures reduce available capacity, while high temperatures accelerate chemical ageing.

## General effects of temperature on batteries
### Battery lifetime and temperature
Higher temperatures generally **shorten battery life**, even if capacity appears higher.

- Low temperatures:
  - reduce usable capacity
  - slow down chemical ageing
- High temperatures:
  - accelerate chemical degradation
  - shorten calendar and cycle life

For lead-acid batteries, lifetime typically **halves for every ~8–10 °C above 25 °C**.

# How Operating Temperature Affects Lithium-Ion Batteries
Temperature plays a major role in battery performance, charging, shelf life and voltage control.

## What is the relationship between battery capacity and temperature?
This can potentially result in a shorter lifespan for devices that depend on batteries as their source of energy, such as smartphones and electric vehicles.

While warmer conditions generally enhance battery performance, prolonged exposure to excessive heat can accelerate aging and compromise the battery’s longevity.

This ensures the battery operates within the prescribed temperature range, promoting longevity, efficiency, and safety.

## Understanding battery types and their optimal temperature range
### What is the impact of extreme temperatures on lithium batteries?
Conversely, high temperatures accelerate the chemical reactions within a lithium-ion battery, which can result in faster aging and a shorter overall lifespan.

In the context of EVs, managing temperature extremes becomes critical for maintaining battery efficiency and lifespan.

## Summary
Temperature significantly affects battery life and performance of lithium-ion batteries. Cold conditions can reduce battery capacity and efficiency, potentially making devices like smartphones and electric cars less reliable, while hot temperatures may appear to improve performance, it can increase the risk of damage and reduce the overall lifespan of the battery.

results.title: How Does Temperature Affect Batteries? - Riello UPS
results.content:
High ambient temperature is the most important factor that influences UPS battery ageing and can cause premature battery failure.

Higher temperatures mean a faster chemical reaction inside the battery, which increases water loss and corrosion.

Valve Regulated Lead-Acid (VRLA) batteries have a rated design life capacity based on an optimum operating temperature of 20-25°C.

For every 10°C constant increase in temperature above this recommendation, it is generally accepted that [battery service life](https://www.riello-ups.com/questions/20-what-does-battery-design-life-mean) will halve (reduce by 50%).

See the below image for an indication how rising ambient temperature can impact service life.

Short-term fluctuations in ambient temperature have relatively little effect on UPS battery lifespan.

Without effective control of the ambient temperature around a battery set, the likelihood of a premature battery failure increases significantly.
